problem: The caption says only the stack and registers sit inside each thread, but the chapter's own list (and the exam trap) also makes the program counter and thread id private to a thread. A student may copy the incomplete list in the exam.
fix: Make each thread node read 'own stack, registers, program counter, thread id' and adjust the caption: 'only the stack, registers, program counter and thread id sit inside each thread; code, data and open files belong to the process.'

problem: 'More threads than cores does not increase speed' is too absolute. Extra threads cannot raise the parallel speedup of CPU-bound work, but they do raise throughput when threads block on I/O (disk, network), which is the reason thread pools exist.
fix: Write: 'More threads than cores does not increase the speedup of CPU-bound work; extra threads help only when some threads block on I/O and the core can switch to another thread.'
